title: Send your work online
concept: git push -u origin main; the website page fills up

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Now send your commits to the website. That is called a **push**.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Use `git push -u origin main` the first time.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: `-u` links your `main` to the remote `main`, so later you can just type `git push`.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Watch the website panel. Your files should appear there.

items.text: Link main to origin/main so plain git push works later

hints: Send your branch to the remote you added, and link the two together.
`git push -u <remote> <branch>` uploads the branch and remembers the pairing.
recap: `git push -u origin main` sends your commits online and links your branch to origin/main. After that, plain `git push` is enough.

cheatSheet.summary: Send main to origin and link them (first time)
Send new commits once the link exists

predict.question: After the push, where do your commits exist?

choices.text: On your laptop and on the website

predict.explanation: Push copies commits. Nothing leaves your laptop. Both copies now have the same history.
